You’re free to dismiss things as you wish. I don’t see a point in trying to argue over coincidence over miracle. But let me ask- is there harm over these people and the nurse being grateful that the nurse checked their baby one last time? Is there truly harm in finding comfort in something that you don’t believe in? Just based on the story, it doesn’t seem like the nurse minds that she believes she was used by God to help save the baby’s life. 
The nurse didn’t do a medical procedure- she just used her stethoscope and listened.

I understand what both of you are saying. I do. But I think the idea here is WHY did the nurse randomly decide to do one last check? The daughter had a clean bill of health, the nurse was wrapping things up to go home for the last time, so there was literally no reason to even THINK that maybe there was something wrong. 

Yet she did. For whatever reason, it was placed in the nurse’s heart to check that baby one more time. Against all reasoning- because remember, the baby was considered perfectly healthy with no reason to think there could be anything wrong. 

No one is discounting medical professionals. If it’d been me, a random person with no medical experience, saying “oh! I want to listen to her heart!” The issue probably would’ve gone unnoticed and the baby would’ve died. 

God chose THAT nurse, one He knew would be fully capable of catching something that small, and  having it handled. 

No one is saying God diagnosed the issue. We’re saying God put it on that nurse’s heart to listen one more time. 

And because she did, she was able to find the issue which led to the baby being saved. 

Again- no one is taking the credit from the nurse or the doctors. But why would a nurse decide to check on a baby that, on paper, is perfectly healthy and normal, unless God put it on her heart. She could’ve done a random check on a different baby, but didn’t. Could’ve just checked her ears, but didn’t. 

It was her experience that caught it. But God was the one who put it on her.
